To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the BRDF of land and ocean surfaces is important in satellite cloud and NO2 trace-gas retrievers, and the geometry-dependent Lambertian-equivalent reflectivity is a simple and effective way to account for the BRD

accounting for the effects of BRDF in satellite retrievals can improve accuracy of the retrieved cloud properties, and that the use of a geometry-dependent LER can improve the accuracy of satellite NO2 retrievals in highly polluted regions.

the use of geometry-dependent LER instead of climatological LERS leads to more realistic cloud and NO2 columns, and that the use of MODIS surface reflectance data in the OMI NO2 algorithms leads to higher NO2 columns.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of the surface BRDF on OMI cloud, aerosol and trace-gas products.
the effects of the BRDF and surface reflectance databases on the accuracy of satellite cloud and trace gas retrievals.
the impact of the BRDF on satellite retrievals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of geometry-dependent LER in the cloud products leads to a more accurate description of cloudiness and, in turn, a better estimation of surface reflectance and trace-gas amounts.
the BRDF effects are important and need to be taken into account, especially for the retrieval of trace-gases, but that they are not the dominant source of error in current algorithms.
the geometry-dependent LER concept, when used in conjunction with the existing OMI algorithms, is a viable and practical approach that can improve OMI retrievals of cloud and NO2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of a geometry-dependent LER in the OMI cloud algorithms leads to a better representation of the cloud fraction, which in turn leads to a better NO2 vertical column retrieval.
the use of the geometry-dependent LER in OMI retrievals improves the accuracy of the derived NO2 columns in polluted areas.
the geometry-dependent LER approach is simple and practical for use in satellite cloud and trace gas retrieval algorithms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
geometry-dependent LER, which can be easily calculated using existing BRDF information, can be readily incorporated into satellite retrievals of cloud, aerosol and trace gases.
the use of geometry-dependent LER can be implemented within existing OMI cloud products and trace-gas retrieval algorithms without major changes.
the BRDF effects should be taken into account in future OMI-based and future satellite-based cloud and trace-gases retrievals.
